issue_context.title: Flume device/entities not created
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I have integrated [Flume](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/flume/) (the water sensor) into my Home Assistant (official HassOS image). The identification worked flawlessly, but there is no device/entities showing up.

![Screenshot from 2022-08-30 20-22-41](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/839552/188240418-de604807-d3a2-4279-b51f-f3d1a203e1a5.png)

Important note, I do have _Flume Insight_ activated on my Flume account.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2022.8.7

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Flume

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/tree/dev/homeassistant/components/flume

### Diagnostics information

No device are created, so no diagnostic information available.

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
Logger: homeassistant.components.sensor
Source: components/flume/sensor.py:62
Integration: Sensor (documentation, issues)
First occurred: 13:28:22 (1 occurrences)
Last logged: 13:28:22

Error while setting up flume platform for sensor
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity_platform.py", line 281, in _async_setup_platform
    await asyncio.shield(task)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/flume/sensor.py", line 62, in async_setup_entry
    device_name = device[KEY_DEVICE_LOCATION][KEY_DEVICE_LOCATION_NAME]
KeyError: 'location'
```


### Additional information

_No response_

Odd... I just tried this on prod and its not working... I'm coming in via nabu-casa - so I probably need to test at home and compare prod to my dev machines... looks like its a token issue with the authentication.

On my dev machine I checked out `2022.9.0` - and everything "seems" to be working... (running in python mode hass -c config)

On my prod machine running i think the same version (but supervised)- i get an auth error... so strange....
Now i noticed in my home assistant directory there is a FLUME_TOKENFILE ... and on the machines they are different...

Issued solved but terribly... i had to delete the FLUME_TOKENFILE-EMAIL from the root of my home assistant directory. I bet this is related to the backing library and I'll need to make a PR or fork the lib if the author isn't around any longer...

I removed that TOKEN file, deleted Flume, and installed the dev branch. There is no `WARNING` log, but the 'ERROR' log reported initially is still there (although at a different line number now in the dev branch)

```bash
    device_timezone = device[KEY_DEVICE_LOCATION][KEY_DEVICE_LOCATION_TIMEZONE]

```

This line in `sensor.py` sounds to hold the issue `device_timezone = device[KEY_DEVICE_LOCATION][KEY_DEVICE_LOCATION_TIMEZONE]`.

The [Flume API](https://flumetech.readme.io/reference/fetch-single-user) might actually return a wrong value for my case. I'm getting down to the `Fetch user` section in their API reference, but then the `user_id` I got from the decoded JWT token generates an error (503 - service unavailable - JWT malformed). Did you ever try to do it just to check? If you can `Fetch user` succesfully, I might just open a ticket in the Flume API itself.
So does it create the sensors with an error? or fail

What that says to me is the return from the API doesn't have `location` in it right?

When I run raw pyflume and get my returns I'm seeing the `location` key in my returns...

Ok, so that's interesting. I ran your code sample but, for any reason, two of my device in the `devices` list does not have the `location` keyword:

```python
for device in devices:
    print(device.keys())

>> dict_keys(['id', 'type', 'location_id', 'bridge_id', 'oriented', 'last_seen', 'connected', 'battery_level', 'product', 'user'])
>> dict_keys(['id', 'type', 'bridge_id', 'oriented', 'last_seen', 'connected', 'battery_level', 'product', 'user', 'location'])

>> dict_keys(['id', 'type', 'bridge_id', 'last_seen', 'connected', 'supports_ap', 'product', 'user', 'location'])
```

I'm not sure why is that, but it sounds like this keyword is not systematically provided by the API.

Also, `devices` lists 4 devices, may be because it does still record my former Flume+bridge that has been replaced by Flume because it was defective.

```python
dict_keys(['id', 'type', 'bridge_id', 'oriented', 'last_seen', 'connected', 'battery_level', 'product', 'user', 'location'])
dict_keys(['id', 'type', 'bridge_id', 'last_seen', 'connected', 'supports_ap', 'product', 'user', 'location'])
```

So I think this is an issue with the backing library most likely... and/or just getting some errors when it tries to process defunct devices... (HOWEVER) I may be able to fix this on the HA side... as well -> only process devices with location dictionary key...

I have double-checked and it is correct that those devices of mine without a `location` keyword are those that are defunct. That makes sense since I remember now that I had to unassigned the 'Home' location of those former devices when I replaced them with the new ones.

I think that provides a good enough rational for your option to skip those devices in HA and prevent future similar issues other users might encounter.
Thats the logic for device processing - so can probably toss in a does it have a location check...
Once you verify I'll put a patch together hopefully
